_comment: Expectations for the ASH CodeCommit pull-request gate regression fixture.
Each expectation carries a 'provenance' field. 'measured' means this exact
value was observed during the 2026-08-28 deploy-validation and is quoted from
real output. 'specified' means it is the behaviour a correct gate must have
but has NOT yet been observed passing - it is the assertion, not a recording.
Do not silently promote a 'specified' value to 'measured'; re-run and record.
The gate's own exit-code-to-verdict mapping, from _verdict() in
deploy/cdk/lib/ash-container-scripts.ts. Duplicated here so the harness
derives verdicts exactly as the gate does rather than inventing its own.

scan_flags._comment: The gate's exact flag set, from CODECOMMIT_GATE_HANDLER.

_comment: These are what turn a passing verdict into trustworthy evidence. The gate
defect this fixture exists to catch produced the RIGHT verdict on the clean
case for the WRONG reason - no scanner ran. A verdict assertion alone
cannot distinguish those two states; these can.
CRITICAL: assert on 'missing', never on 'skipped'. SKIPPED means a scanner
was deliberately not selected, which is the mechanism sharding uses to
exclude scanners (core/phases/scan_phase.py). A fixture that required
skipped == 0 would break every sharded run. MISSING means selected but its
dependencies were absent; ERROR means it ran and failed. Only those two are
faults.
_do_not_key_on_has_issues: validation_summary.*.has_issues LOOKS like the signal for this and is NOT.
MEASURED 2026-08-28, on a run with four scanner tools absent:
False, with four selected scanners that never ran. 'expected' counts only
scanners actually DISPATCHED, so a MISSING scanner never enters the expected
set and cannot register as missing from it. The field under-reports exactly
the condition it appears to report.
A fix keyed on has_issues would review well, pass a test written against the
same assumption, and do nothing. Key on summary_stats.missing and on the
per-scanner status. has_issues is checked here as an ADVISORY line only and
never as a reason a case fails; assert_case.py --selftest has a dedicated
case that fails if it ever becomes load-bearing.
Why this was nearly missed: the first run to examine this had missing=0, so
both fields agreed and the data could not distinguish them. Two signals that
agree on the run in front of you tell you nothing about whether they are

cases.name: vulnerable
cases.description: Adds src/vulnerable.py with bandit HIGH findings. Must be blocked.

expected_sarif_rule_ids._comment: Rule id -> SARIF level, as observed. B404 is note/LOW and is below the MEDIUM threshold, so it is reported but not actionable.

measured_on.where: locally, in the deployed gate image, all filesystems writable
measured_on.note: In Lambda the SAME image and flags produced exit 0 and verdict 'passed' with 5 of 10 scanners MISSING/ERROR. That is the defect.

cases.name: clean
cases.description: Adds src/safe_math.py with no findings. Must pass, and must pass for the right reason.
not_measured_because: The local run of this case was blocked by the operator's permission
system during the 2026-08-28 validation, so its local exit code was never
observed. In Lambda it returned verdict 'passed' - but so did the
vulnerable case, with an identical all-MISSING/ERROR scanner table, so
that observation is worthless as confirmation. Run the harness to record

_comment: The conjunction that pins the defect: a passing verdict is legitimate ONLY
when no scanner is MISSING or ERROR. Checkable against any
(verdict, scanner-table) pair, so it needs no AWS, no Docker and no working
scanner set -- it replays a recorded observation.
This is deliberately NOT the same assertion as integrity_invariants above.
That one says 'the scanners must have run'; it can only be evaluated on a
live scan. This one says 'if they did not run, do not claim green', which is
evaluable on a record and is the property the gate actually violated.
WHY IT SURVIVES THE FIX: post-fix, the same scanner table must produce a
non-passing verdict. Only expected_verdict_after_fix below changes; the
invariant, the recorded table and the harness all stay as they are.
Until the exit-code fix lands this replay is EXPECTED TO FAIL, and the
harness reports it as XFAIL rather than as a red test, so it does not read
as noise and get muted. When it starts passing, that is the signal the fix
landed -- the harness reports XPASS and tells you to flip this flag.
Do not delete the case at that point; flipping the flag keeps it guarding
against a re-regression.
known_defect.tracking: ASH _compute_exit_code derives the exit code from finding counts only and never reads scanner status; core/unified_metrics.py treats MISSING as passed
known_defect.fix_must_key_on: metadata.summary_stats.missing (and/or per-scanner scanner_results.<name>.status), NOT validation_summary.*.has_issues -- see _do_not_key_on_has_issues above

_comment: The single most important assertion. During validation BOTH cases reported
'passed'. A gate that returns one verdict for all inputs is broken
regardless of which verdict it picks, and only comparing the two cases
reveals it. Neither case alone can.

observed_broken_state.scanner_table: bandit MISSING, checkov MISSING, detect-secrets ERROR, opengrep ERROR, semgrep MISSING
